Public GitHub repository. Pages deployment is configured but blocked by an account billing lock; no live provider/OS acceptance claim. No automatic second-vault copy. Noncommercial source-available license.

<p align="center"><em>Turn a captured page into a reviewed, source-preserving Obsidian note.</em></p>

<p align="center">Planned Pages URL (deployment pending): `https://cassiohenriqueofc.github.io/obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit/`</p>

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a community template toolkit for the official Obsidian Web Clipper. It is not the Obsidian extension. Interpreter execution stays manual; generated notes keep the source content supplied by the Clipper.

## What this project does

Import a JSON template, capture a page with [Obsidian Web Clipper](https://obsidian.md/clipper), optionally run its Interpreter yourself, review the result, and save a structured Markdown note. The templates separate source evidence from model-generated explanations and preserve the supplied `{{content}}` in the note.

Use these when you want **Obsidian Web Clipper templates**, **manual AI interpretation**, **source-preserving web capture**, or **structured Markdown notes** without automatic Interpreter execution.

## Choose a template

| Template | Best for | Interpreter prompts | Original content |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| [Balanced](templates/01-balanced-original-callout-clipper.json) | Explanations, research ideas, and a project brief | 6 | Expandable source callout |
| [Compact](templates/02-compact-original-footer-clipper.json) | A shorter analysis with source near the bottom | 4 | Footer section |
| [Archive](templates/03-source-archive-clipper.json) | Deterministic capture without AI | 0 | Source callout |

All generated text is English. Copyable output uses fenced blocks; interactive Obsidian tasks stay outside fences. The archive style does not need a model.

<details open>
<summary>See how page evidence becomes an organized note</summary>

</details>

The static OpenGraph artwork remains in [`assets/social-preview.jpg`](assets/social-preview.jpg); this animation adds a step-by-step explanation for the README and interactive site.

## Quick start

1. Install [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/download) and the official [Web Clipper](https://obsidian.md/clipper).
2. Create a `clippings` folder in your vault.
3. Import a JSON file from [`templates/`](templates/).
4. Set the vault and folder in the template. Keep automatic Interpreter execution disabled.
5. For the two analysis templates, click **Interpret** manually, review the note, then save it. Do not run Interpreter for Archive.

The supplied content can be a page selection or highlights rather than a complete article. The template retains the `{{content}}` value it receives; the extension, browser, or page may limit what is captured.

### Optional local customization

Run these commands from the project folder with Python 3.10 or newer. The generated files stay in the ignored `local-only/` folder.

```powershell
py -3 scripts/configure_templates.py --vault "My Vault" --folder "clippings"
```

```bash
python3 scripts/configure_templates.py --vault "My Vault" --folder "clippings"
```

Then import the customized files from `local-only/templates/`. See the [Windows, macOS, and Linux instructions](docs/en-US/install.md) for details.

## Compatibility and status

The project owner reported Web Clipper 1.7.1 and Obsidian 1.15.1 on Windows. That baseline was used for isolated template-renderer checks, not a complete installed-extension acceptance test. Full save checks on Windows, macOS, and Linux and live Interpreter-provider calls remain unverified.

This is a public release. GitHub Pages deployment is configured at [the project URL](https://cassiohenriqueofc.github.io/obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit/). GitHub Actions is currently blocked because GitHub reports an account billing lock; the site is not live until that is resolved and deployment succeeds. The configured build uses canonical URLs, Open Graph and Twitter metadata, JSON-LD, a sitemap, and indexable robots rules for deployment once GitHub Actions is available. The custom license prohibits commercial use without separate permission; it is source-available, not OSI-approved open source.

## Help and contributions

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before proposing changes. Report security issues using [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not commit personal vault paths, settings exports, API keys, or private notes.

# Capture specification

- Baseline: Web Clipper 1.7.1 and Obsidian 1.15.1; user reported, not fully live-tested.
- Template language: English. Documentation languages: en-US and pt-BR.
- Execution: always manual Interpreter; no template can enforce the global setting alone.
- Tracked destination: Demo Vault / clippings. Private customization is ignored by Git.
- Optional copy: manual copy of saved Markdown; no automatic dual-vault save claimed.
- Formatting: separate foldable callouts with one structural > prefix. No authored
  > > nesting. Prefix blank lines and code fences as well as content lines.
- Copyable explanations, source evidence, and briefs are fenced. Interactive
  tasks are outside fences inside their callout.
- Original content variable is not sliced. It can represent page extraction,
  selection, or highlights; it does not guarantee full-page or video access.
- Model evidence is bounded: Markdown 24000, HTML 8000, JSON-LD 12000 characters.
- Preserve uncertainty; no invented external search results or existing vault links.
- Preserve a deterministic Archive option for provider failures and syntax-heavy sources.
- Source-preservation limit: literal Clipper expressions can be reprocessed in AI
  variants in 1.7.1. Prefer Archive without Interpreter for such source pages.


# Search and repository presentation review — 2026-11-18

## Positioning

Preferred display name: **Obsidian Web Clipper Toolkit**.
Repository slug: **obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit**. The owner has now renamed the
public GitHub repository; the previous `obsidian-web-cliper` spelling omitted a
`p`. The project remains a community template toolkit, not an official Obsidian
extension.

Recommended GitHub About description:

> Source-preserving Obsidian Web Clipper templates for manual AI interpretation and structured Markdown notes.

Recommended page description:

> Capture webpages with Obsidian Web Clipper templates, run interpretation prompts manually, and save source-preserving Markdown notes with structured callouts.

Use these phrases naturally where they describe the actual project: **Obsidian
Web Clipper templates**, **manual AI interpretation**, **source-preserving web
capture**, **Markdown notes**, and **knowledge management**. Do not repeat them as
keyword lists or promise rank positions.

## Search findings

The official Obsidian Web Clipper repository describes the extension as a way to
highlight and capture web pages in a browser. Public GitHub search results also
show multiple community repositories labeled as Web Clipper template collections.
The toolkit should therefore distinguish its purpose: English prompts run only
when the user starts Interpreter manually; supplied source content remains in the
saved note; and one template offers capture without model interpretation.

This review is a qualitative search-result and repository-page review. It does
not include Google Keyword Planner volume, Google Search Console performance, or
stable star/fork rankings. The repository is now public; search ranking and indexing results still require time and Search Console data.

## Current implementation

- The root README uses the generated banner, language links, a template table, quick-start commands, example links, navigation, and a prominent animated feature flow.
- Seven language READMEs and seven language pages are linked from the project.
- The site builder creates locale-specific titles/descriptions, absolute canonical URLs, seven `hreflang` alternates plus `x-default`, Open Graph/Twitter metadata, and `SoftwareSourceCode` JSON-LD. The indexable build includes crawlable robots rules and a sitemap. The language chooser and 404 are noindex and excluded from the sitemap.
- The new static Open Graph/Twitter preview is 1200 × 630 JPEG. The original banner and animated workflow remain distinct assets. The animation is not used as social preview.
- Sitemap `lastmod` is drawn from the reviewed Proposal date. Keep that date aligned with content changes; omit `changefreq` and `priority`, which Google ignores.
- GitHub Pages is configured at the repository URL, but the site is not live: GitHub Actions is blocked by an account billing lock, the Pages API returned 403, and the deployed URL returned 404 during the prior check. The owner authorized publishing and indexing; deployment still needs a successful workflow.
- No stars, trending badges, contributor totals, or release counts are hard-coded. Do not claim rankings, indexing, or rich results.
- GitHub confirms that the repository is public and template-enabled. The connected API returned HTTP 403 for About-description and topic changes; browser settings access was unavailable. The repository description remains its earlier wording.

## Publication controls

After publication:

1. Review the entire Git diff, release ZIP, settings, and privacy scan.
2. The canonical URL is the GitHub Pages project URL. Confirm a successful deploy before treating it as live or requesting indexing.
3. Verify titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, language alternates, social image,
   JSON-LD, robots policy, and sitemap on the live site. Register and verify the
   property in Google Search Console before requesting indexing.
4. GitHub topic tags are still pending because the connected settings API and browser UI could not update them.
5. The GitHub social-preview image remains a manual Settings item; use `assets/social-preview-1200x630.jpg`. The animated feature flow is separate and available in the README/site.
6. Do not add an `FAQPage` rich-result strategy: Google removed FAQ rich results
   in May 2026. Keep helpful FAQ prose only if it answers real user questions.

Google says its generative search features do not require special schema.org
markup, and `llms.txt` does not change Google Search visibility or rankings.
Structured data remains useful for describing the software and can make eligible
pages qualify for supported search features; it does not guarantee a rich result.

## Technical corrections (2026-11-18)

The reusable, Obsidian-ready reference is [SEO signals and website proposal playbook](seo-signals-and-indexing-playbook.md). It includes the current indexing state, page metadata, platform mockups, and a proposal checklist.

The supplied SEO notes mixed a personal portfolio identity and the personal domain with this toolkit. They were not imported: the repository has its own GitHub Pages URL and no authorized custom domain. The notes' recommendations were checked against the actual static Python build instead of treating their personal-site instructions as project requirements.

Google guidance does not require special markup for AI Overviews/AI features; structured data must describe visible content and does not guarantee enhanced results. `llms.txt` has no documented Google ranking effect. `robots.txt` is not a way to remove an already indexed URL. A meta refresh is not an HTTP 301; GitHub Pages does not provide server-side redirects or custom response headers. The toolkit now uses a custom 404 page, but legacy redirects remain unavailable without a separate redirect service.

Before indexing: restore Actions billing, verify a successful deployment and live metadata, verify site ownership in Search Console/Bing, then submit the sitemap. These operations require working GitHub/account access and were not performed in this local SEO change.

## How the current SEO setup works

The static builder is scripts/build_site.py. It writes one HTML page per locale and, for the indexable build, emits crawl metadata, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml.

| Signal | Purpose | Current implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page title and visible H1 | State the page topic and language | Descriptive titles and headings for each locale |
| Meta description | Offer a concise summary that may become a search snippet | One description per locale; Google may choose page text instead |
| Canonical | Identify the preferred URL for equivalent content | Absolute canonical URL per locale route |
| hreflang and x-default | Connect language alternatives | Seven locale routes plus x-default |
| Open Graph | Supply title, description, URL, type and image for share cards | Unique title/description, canonical URL, static 1200 × 630 image, alt text and dimensions |
| Twitter Card | Supply X card type and matching share fields | summary_large_image, title, description, image and alt text |
| JSON-LD SoftwareSourceCode | Describe the toolkit in machine-readable form | Uses known project facts; does not guarantee rich results |
| robots.txt | State crawl policy and sitemap location | Indexable build allows crawling and lists the sitemap |
| noindex,follow | Keep selected HTML pages out of search while leaving links followable | Root language chooser and 404 page |
| Sitemap | Help crawlers discover canonical routes | Seven locale pages only; lastmod uses the Proposal date |
| Custom 404 | Help visitors recover from a missing route | site/404.html; effective after Pages is deployed |

The sitemap lastmod value must reflect a real significant page update. This
project derives it from the reviewed Proposal date; update that date when
substantive documented content changes. Google ignores changefreq and priority,
so the generator omits them.

llms.txt is a navigation aid for clients that choose to use it. Do not present
it as a Google ranking signal or an AI search requirement. Google says standard
Search fundamentals apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode; no special schema.org
markup is needed for those features.

### Discovery and preview flow

> [!NOTE]+ Indexing is a sequence, not a switch
> A metadata change does not instantly create a search result. A page must be
> reachable, crawled, eligible, selected for indexing, and then rendered by a
> search product. Each stage may be delayed or declined.

> ~~~mermaid
> flowchart LR
>   A["Proposal and page content"] --> B["Build static HTML"]
>   B --> C["Live HTTPS page"]
>   C --> D["Crawler can fetch page"]
>   D --> E["Canonical and language signals processed"]
>   E --> F["Index decision"]
>   F --> G["Google or Bing result"]
>   F --> H["AI search may cite page"]
>   C --> I["Social crawler reads Open Graph"]
>   I --> J["Link preview card"]
>   C --> K["GitHub repository metadata"]
>   K --> L["GitHub repository search and README"]
>   X["Current blocker: Pages returns 404"] -. blocks .-> C
> ~~~

For this project, the path stops before “Live HTTPS page.” The metadata is in
the generated files, but the configured Pages URL currently returns 404.

### Content-to-metadata build graph

> [!NOTE]+ Keep SEO fields tied to approved page content
> Proposal facts feed the route copy and metadata. The build should derive
> structured data from the same evidence, then validation checks the generated
> result before deployment.

> ~~~mermaid
> flowchart TB
>   P["Reviewed website proposal"] --> R["Route and locale content"]
>   R --> G["Static site generator"]
>   I["Approved identity and project facts"] --> G
>   A["Share image and alt text"] --> G
>   G --> H["HTML title, description, canonical, hreflang"]
>   G --> S["Open Graph, X Card, JSON-LD"]
>   G --> C["robots.txt and sitemap.xml"]
>   H --> V["Local validation and preview review"]
>   S --> V
>   C --> V
>   V --> D["Deployment after access is ready"]
>   D --> M["Search Console, Bing, and social preview checks"]
> ~~~

## Search and sharing preview mockups

These examples use the project's current English metadata and show where it
could appear after deployment. They are mockups, not actual indexed results.
Search engines and social platforms control their final text, cropping, caches,
and display; they may rewrite or omit fields.

### Google organic result

> [!EXAMPLE]+ Google Search mockup
> ~~~text
> Obsidian Web Clipper Toolkit
> cassiohenriqueofc.github.io › obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit › en-US
> Web Clipper templates with source-preserving AI notes | Obsidian Web Clipper Toolkit
> Use Obsidian Web Clipper templates to capture webpages, run AI interpretation
> manually, and save structured Markdown notes that preserve the source content.
> ~~~

Google may build the title link from page titles, headings, prominent text,
Open Graph title, and links. It usually selects snippet text from the page and
may use the meta description when it better matches the query.

### Google AI result

> [!EXAMPLE]+ Possible citation layout
> ~~~text
> AI Overview
> [Answer assembled by Google from selected sources]
>
> Sources
> [Obsidian Web Clipper Toolkit]  [Another selected source]
> ~~~

This is only a layout illustration. There is no guarantee that an AI result
will appear, cite this site, or use these words.

### Bing result

> [!EXAMPLE]+ Bing Search mockup
> ~~~text
> Web Clipper templates with source-preserving AI notes
> https://cassiohenriqueofc.github.io/obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit/en-US/
> Use Obsidian Web Clipper templates to capture webpages, run AI interpretation
> manually, and save structured Markdown notes that preserve the source content.
> ~~~

Bing chooses its own final result text. After deployment, verify the property
and sitemap in Bing Webmaster Tools.

> ~~~text

> Source-preserving Obsidian Web Clipper templates for manual AI interpretation
> and structured Markdown notes.
> Topics: obsidian · web-clipper · markdown · templates · knowledge-management
> ~~~
> The repository is public. The About text and topics above are recommendations,
> not confirmed live settings. GitHub search can consider repository name,
> description, topics, and README contents.

## Where results can appear

| Destination | Main input | How to check after deployment | Current state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Search | Crawlable HTML, internal links, canonical, title, page content | Search Console URL Inspection and sitemap report; a site: query is only a probe | Not live or verified |
| Google AI Overviews / AI Mode | Search-eligible pages and helpful content; no special AI markup | Search Console reports where available; inspect actual citations | No site listing verified; citation is not guaranteed |
| Bing Search | Crawlable page and sitemap | Bing Webmaster Tools URL Inspection and sitemap report | Not live or verified |
| GitHub repository search | Repository name, About description, topics, README | Search with in:name, in:description, in:topics, and in:readme | Public repo; About/topics are pending |
| Facebook / LinkedIn / chat previews | Open Graph values and reachable image | LinkedIn Post Inspector and platform share preview/debug tools | Untested; Pages is unavailable |
| X | Twitter Card and Open Graph values; accessible image | Inspect the post composer or current card preview tool | Untested; Pages is unavailable |
| GitHub repo share card | Separate image in repository Settings | Open repository page and inspect its preview | Image ready; setting pending |

A GitHub repository page and a GitHub Pages website are separate. Repo About,
topics, and repository social preview do not replace the website's canonical,
sitemap, Open Graph, or Twitter metadata.

## Reusable proposal-driven workflow

### 1. Gather verified proposal facts

Record real, owner-approved answers before implementation:

- Project or organization name and one-sentence purpose
- Audience, user problem, actual services and deliverables
- Primary language and every supported locale
- Canonical domain and hosting platform; label planned versus verified
- Route list, navigation, and page purpose
- Approved public identity and contact information
- Repository, license, maintainer, and verified social accounts
- Primary user action and accurate call to action
- Real screenshots/share art, source, ownership, dimensions, and alt text
- Privacy, analytics, consent, form handling, and retention rules
- Webmaster account owner authorized to verify the property
- Build, tests, release, access, and deployment constraints

Do not invent facts, testimonials, traffic, awards, affiliations, dates, addresses,
schema fields, or search-volume claims. Keep secrets, personal settings exports,
and unrelated personal-site content out of a public repository.

### 2. Plan each route

For every indexable URL, record its locale, purpose, page title, visible H1,
unique description, canonical URL, language alternates, internal links, crawl
policy, sitemap inclusion, and structured data facts. Plan share title,
description, URL, image path, dimensions, and accessible alt text. Use
structured data only when it accurately matches visible content.

### 3. Build and audit locally

1. Inspect generated HTML; ensure metadata appears in the initial response.
2. Check URL host, casing, trailing slash, canonical, locales, status codes,
   redirects, and 404 behavior.
3. Parse JSON-LD and compare every field with visible, approved content.
4. Check robots policy and sitemap routes; exclude noindex and 404 pages.
5. Open the preview image URL; confirm HTTPS, file type, dimensions, file size,
   alt text, and safe cropping.
6. Test keyboard access, mobile layout, headings, performance, and image sizes.
7. Check links and remove broken download, navigation, and preview URLs.
8. Scan for secrets, personal paths, unapproved email addresses, and claims.
9. Record commands and results; label local checks separately from live checks.

### 4. Publish and verify

1. Confirm owner authorization, domain, HTTPS, hosting, and deployment access.
2. Deploy reviewed source and inspect the workflow run.
3. Fetch the public page, image, robots.txt, sitemap, canonical routes, and 404.
4. Verify ownership in Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
5. Submit the live sitemap and inspect priority URLs.
6. Test social previews in platform tools; allow for cache refresh delays.
7. Monitor crawl issues, queries, and performance; save date-stamped evidence.
8. Update the Proposal, changelog, SEO note, and handoff after each session.

A sitemap helps discovery; it does not guarantee crawling, indexing, ranking, or
AI citations. A crawl request is not a guarantee. A noindex directive must be
crawlable so that a crawler can see it; do not block that page in robots.txt when
you rely on its noindex tag.

## Copy-ready SEO section for a new website proposal

> [!SUMMARY]+ Website search, indexing, and sharing plan
> Replace each placeholder with a verified fact. Mark unknown values as pending.
>
> ~~~markdown
> ## Search, indexing, and share-preview plan
>
> - Project name:
> - Purpose and audience:
> - User need and primary action:
> - Canonical domain:
> - Hosting and deployment method:
> - Routes and page purpose:
> - Primary language and locale routes:
> - Approved public organization/person facts:
> - Contact and social links:
> - Indexing policy by route:
> - Sitemap and robots.txt:
> - Page titles and descriptions:
> - Canonical and hreflang rules:
> - Structured data type and evidence per property:
> - Open Graph and X card title, description, and URL:
> - Preview image path, source, dimensions, format, and alt:
> - Accessibility and mobile requirements:
> - Analytics, consent, privacy, and retention:
> - Search Console / Bing property owner:
> - Local validation steps:
> - Deployment acceptance checks:
> - Unverified facts:
> - Risks, blockers, and dependencies:
> - Session owner and next review date:
> ~~~

# Publishing and indexing

[Português](../pt-BR/publishing.md) · [Home](../../README.md)

## Deployment status

The owner authorized public indexing and GitHub Pages deployment at:

`https://cassiohenriqueofc.github.io/obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit/`

The workflow is configured, but GitHub Actions has not started because the account is billing-locked. The Pages API also returned 403. The site is not live; do not submit its sitemap or claim indexing until a successful deployment is verified.

## Generated SEO signals

The indexable build emits a unique title and description for each of seven locale pages, absolute canonical URLs, `hreflang` links plus `x-default`, Open Graph and Twitter image metadata, and `SoftwareSourceCode` JSON-LD. The social image is a static 1200 × 630 JPEG; the animated workflow image is separate. The language chooser and 404 page are `noindex,follow` and are excluded from the sitemap. `robots.txt` permits crawling and names the sitemap in the indexable build. Sitemap `lastmod` uses the reviewed Proposal date; update that date when the documented project content changes.

These signals help crawlers understand and preview pages; they do not guarantee ranking, indexing, or rich results. `llms.txt` is a navigation aid for compatible clients, not a Google ranking feature. JSON-LD describes the project and is not a special requirement for AI search.

## Build and verify

```bash
python3 scripts/build_site.py --base-url https://cassiohenriqueofc.github.io/obsidian-web-clipper-toolkit/ --indexable
python3 scripts/validate.py
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site
```

The builder does not deploy. After Actions billing is restored, run the workflow, verify all locale URLs, metadata, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, and 404 behavior. Then verify ownership in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools and submit the live sitemap. Search Console verification tokens and owner account access are not stored in this repository.

GitHub's repository About text, topics, and social preview are separate Settings fields. The recommended About description is recorded in [the SEO review](../../project/seo-review.md); these settings have not been changed. No custom domain is configured.
